Timecode Generator (LTC) (experimental — now its own tool)

Runs as a separate page so it can keep going on its own and target a dedicated output on a multi-output sound card. Open Timecode Generator ↗
Space start/pause   T hold to talk (Crew Talk voice)   R reset   F fullscreen this window   ←→ previous/next cue   Drag the Extended Display window onto your second screen, then press F11 for true full screen.
1-5 message presets (5 MIN/PLACES/STANDBY/GO/HOLD)   6 clear message   7 flash toggle   8 open extended display   9 test alarm   0 save show — handy if you're driving this from a Stream Deck or other macro pad: map each button to the matching key with its plain "Hotkey" action, no plugin needed. Just make sure this browser tab is the focused window when a button is pressed.
Stage Manager Countdown Timer — built for Stage Effects Group (Pty) Ltd. Runs entirely offline in this browser tab.
To share a broadcast: the link is already set up — just click Start Broadcasting, then copy the link that appears just below the buttons and send it (WhatsApp, email, whatever's easiest). Viewers just open it, no login or app needed. Every field in that box is still editable if you want your own link instead. Running several shows on different computers? Each one generates its own separate link automatically, so just copy the one shown on that computer.
Save Show / Load Show (top of the Running Order list) now saves your cue list as an Excel (.xlsx) file — open it, edit it, or hand it to someone else, then Load Show it back in. Load Show still opens older .json show files too, and can open a running order built from scratch in Excel (a "Type"/"Name" table with Minutes/Seconds columns). Loading always replaces the current list, so save first if you want to keep it.

Advanced settings (custom hosting, your own Firebase project, direct links)
Voice Relay (TURN) Server (fixes Crew Talk voice not connecting across different networks)
Crew Talk voice connects device-to-device directly by default, which works fine when everyone's on the same Wi-Fi — but it can fail to connect at all when people are on different networks (e.g. one on venue Wi-Fi, one on mobile data). A TURN relay server fixes this. Free ones are available from providers like Metered.ca or Twilio — paste what they give you below. Leave blank to use direct connections only.
